truth: Black Marsh—Argonia to its people—is a vast subtropical basin of slow rivers, tidal deltas, peat domes, and flooded root-tangles fed by the Niben's spill and the warm rains of the Padomaic Ocean. Only its north-western rim rises into firm basalt and limestone; everywhere else dry ground consists of natural levees, shell middens, ancient stone xanmeer platforms, and clay mounds raised around sentient Hist trees. Before the Duskfall, Saxhleel priest-kings built calendar pyramids and stone canals; after the Duskfall they abandoned stone for reed, mud, and living root, listening to the Hist sap while empires and Dunmer slavers broke their teeth on the outer border and never reached Helstrom at the centre.

shadowfen.truth: Shadowfen is the north-western border mire where Morrowind's ash-runoff meets Argonia's deep peat: a scarred frontier of broken slaver chains, mud-stilt villages, sunken step-pyramids, and vigilant border-tribes watching every road down from Deshaan. Here former Dres captives and Tree-Minders guard the Percolating Mire and Alten Corimont against smuggling rings that still try to spirit hatchlings north across the hills. Beneath the pitcher bogs and cypress knees lie Barsaebic Ayleid ruins and the twin-peaked xanmeer of Ten-Maur-Wolk, where water-locks still answer the old calendar.

stormhold.truth: Built atop the only high basalt and limestone shelf on the northern frontier, Stormhold wraps Argonian mud-and-timber compounds around the half-sunken white-stone spires of a Barsaebic Ayleid citadel. It is the northern gateway of Black Marsh, where raised stone causeways meet the Morrowind and Cyrodiil roads and where caravans trade northern iron and wetland grain for marsh reagents, bog-timber and cured hides. Tree-Minders share the market ring with Dunmer and Imperial factors, while beneath the city's guildhalls and plazas, flooded Ayleid crystal vaults and Shadowscale training sanctums run deep into the living rock.

gideon.truth: Gideon is the western reed-plain bordering Cyrodiil's Blackwood: a country of wide sawgrass prairies, Niben overflow marshes, half-drowned Imperial causeways, and fortified stone manors left from the Colovian and Septim occupations. Its walled seat of Gideon and the ruined penal fortress of Blackrose stand on the last firm silt levees before the deep interior swamp begins. Here assimilated Lukiul townsfolk, Imperial charter-traders, and An-Xileel traditionalists contest every bridge, punt-ferry and warehouse, while weathered chapels stand beside living Hist pools and blood-root cults and bog hounds haunt the sunken estates.

helstrom.truth: Two worlds share this central and eastern region: along the Padomaic barrier spits stand Thorn and Archon, hybrid ports of call for coastal traders and former slaver houses; inland lies the impenetrable root-labyrinth surrounding Helstrom, the sacred capital no outsider army has ever taken. In Helstrom, giant interlocking Hist roots form living bridges over dark water, and the eldest Tree-Minders commune with the root-heart of Argonia. When a rogue syndicate taps a deep root-vein in the east, the central trees stir and summon the interior tribes.

lilmoth.truth: Where the southern river channels fan out into Topal Bay stands Lilmoth: a bustling, half-sunken delta port of rotting Imperial stone warehouses, cypress stilt-quays, smuggling wharves, and a customhouse that taxes everything that floats. In the surrounding tidal mangrove bayous, silver-hulled Kothringi plague-ships from the Second Era Knahaten Flu still drift through the warm salt fog, and pre-Duskfall xanmeer steps lie just beneath the brackish tide. Saxhleel punt-men, Khajiit smugglers, Padomaic spice factors, and An-Xileel dock-wardens share the lantern-lit boardwalks at night.

murkmire.truth: Murkmire is the deep south-eastern coastal shelf stretching from Soulrest's sheltered sound to the outer mangrove archipelagos: a vertical jungle of stilt-roots, bright-painted tribal villages, acid sinkhole fens, and the grandest pre-Duskfall xanmeer pyramids rising out of the warm equatorial mist. Here the welcoming Bright-Throat artisan clans and the fierce Dead-Water hunter-warriors keep the old Saxhleel ways untouched by Imperial law, carving root-canoes, mixing rare marsh venoms, and reading the stone calendars of Xul-Thuxis and the Teeth of Sithis while Shadowscale initiates undergo their silent trials in the flooded depths.

The Hist are sacred sentient elders; Saxhleel never fell or mill living Hist trees

Black Marsh's ancient stone layer is pre-Duskfall Saxhleel xanmeer and Barsaebic Ayleid, never Dwemer
